items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: so we formed this trio, Jane Jarvis, Earl May and myself.

ctx.x: Bill Berry’s there also. So it’s funny how everything comes full circle. Anyway we ate and we found out we enjoyed each other’s company. I found her utterly delightful and the things she likes. So we kind of kept in touch. I’ve sort of had a crusade really, to get some acknowledgement or recognition for her, so we formed this trio, Jane Jarvis, Earl May and myself. And we played at Zinno’s and when I go down to Ft. Lauderdale, I think when my little stage patter, I’ll say that when I was asked to join this band,…
So Earl May’s on the gig too, right?

items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: I just made a record date with Jane [Jarvis] and Benny and Grady. [Tate].

ctx.x: I’m still that way. I just made a record date with Jane [Jarvis] and Benny and Grady. [Tate]. And at the end of the date she treated us financially very well. So I put the check in my pocket and I told Benny I said, “Ah, Benny, I’ve got some money, I can start tipping again.” He fell on the floor. Because I do that a lot. I feel that that’s what it’s for, to share a little bit. People are working and giving you a service, you treat them nice. So I went right down to the garage and took my car, I gave that guy a…
Well now I know why everybody says nice things about you.
